comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose that their accelerated computing data center platforms are founded on GPUs and have expanded to include other accelerators like DPUs. NVDA states its platform is founded on GPUs and expanded to include DPUs and CPUs, allowing optimization across the computing stack. AMD similarly lists GPUs and DPUs among its Data Center segment products, leveraging these technologies to address AI workload acceleration needs. However, NVDA explicitly highlights the recent expansion into CPUs in FY2024 as a key platform evolution, whereas AMD's disclosure frames the combination of CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs as a portfolio approach to optimize performance and power for diverse workloads.

sentences.text: At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.
Beyond GPUs, our data center platform expanded to include DPUs in fiscal year 2022 and CPUs in fiscal year 2024.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (avgo_2024_1_D009, avgo_2024_1_D010) focus on networking solutions (NICs, switching) and custom silicon (ASICs) respectively. They do not disclose a foundational accelerated computing platform built on GPUs or a similar portfolio of general-purpose accelerators (like CPUs/GPUs/DPUs) comparable to NVDA's core platform hardware foundation. AVGO's disclosures address data movement and customer-specific ASICs rather than a proprietary general-purpose accelerated computing architecture.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond CPUs, Intel delivers xPU products including GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and accelerators to address diverse workloads and computing needs. The company aims to offer leading products across these different architectural categories.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and Intel describe a strategy of offering a diverse portfolio of hardware accelerators beyond just CPUs to address different workloads. NVDA describes its accelerated computing platform founded on GPUs, which also includes DPUs and CPUs. Intel describes its 'xPU approach' which encompasses client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators beyond the CPU. Both companies aim to provide leading products across these architectural categories to meet diverse computing needs, highlighting a similar diversification from traditional CPU-only offerings to a broader 'xPU' or accelerated computing ecosystem.

sentences.text: At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.
They are available in the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform and in industry standard servers from every major cloud provider and server maker.
Beyond the CPU, we deliver a family of xPU products encompassing client and data center GPUs, IPUs, FPGAs, and other accelerators.
The xPU approach recognizes that different workloads benefit from different computing architectures, and our broad portfolio helps meet our customers' increasingly diverse computing needs.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (mu_2024_1_D040, mu_2024_1_D016) focus exclusively on storage solutions (SSDs, NAND) for AI and high-performance computing workloads. They do not disclose accelerated computing platforms, GPUs, or processing accelerators comparable to NVDA's core hardware foundation.

The retrieved candidates (qcom_2024_1_D029, qcom_2024_1_D034) describe mobile and consumer-focused System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures (Snapdragon) primarily for devices like PCs, smartphones, and automotive systems. NVDA's disclosure focuses on data center-scale accelerated computing platforms. The form factors, target markets, and specific hardware components (mobile SoCs vs. data center GPUs/DPUs) are fundamentally different.
